questions.text:
"From where are they bringing their books? _______ bringing _______ books from ________"

The words that best fill the blanks in the above sentence are
questions.solution:
"They're (they are) bringing their (belonging to them) books from there (that place)."

Answer: They're, their, there

questions.text: The area of a square is [latex]d[/latex]. What is the area of the circle which has the diagonal of the square as its diameter?
questions.solution:
Side s with [latex]s^2=d[/latex]. Diagonal = [latex]s\sqrt2[/latex], so the circle's radius is [latex]\frac{s}{\sqrt2}[/latex].
Area = [latex]\pi\frac{s^2}{2}=\frac12\pi d[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\frac12\pi d[/latex]

questions.text:
What would be the smallest natural number which when divided either by 20 or by 42
or by 76 leaves a remainder of 7 in each case?
questions.solution:
LCM(20, 42, 76) = [latex]2^2\times3\times5\times7\times19=7980[/latex]. Remainder 7 in each case: 7980 + 7 = 7987.

Answer: 7987

questions.text:
What is the missing number in the following sequence?
2, 12, 60, 240, 720, 1440, _____ ,0
questions.solution:
Each term is multiplied by 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0 in turn: 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 6 = 12, [latex]\times[/latex] 5 = 60, [latex]\times[/latex] 4 = 240, [latex]\times[/latex] 3 = 720, [latex]\times[/latex] 2 = 1440, [latex]\times[/latex] 1 = 1440, [latex]\times[/latex] 0 = 0.

Answer: 1440
